paragraphs: As of Friday, October 2, before the U.S. open, the Nasdaq enters payroll Friday with a resilient tape but an unusually difficult rates backdrop. The Nasdaq Composite recovered from a sharp intraday selloff on Thursday to finish 0.04% higher, while the S&P 500 gained 0.20%. The important move was underneath the indexes: the U.S. 10-year Treasury yield surged as high as 5.342%, its highest level since 2002, before retreating as the session progressed. That reversal allowed technology shares to stabilize, while strong AI-related demand signals around Micron and record Korean semiconductor exports continued to support the structural semiconductor story.

The counterweight is that the long end of the Treasury market remains the dominant valuation risk for Nasdaq. Oil also jumped more than 4% Thursday, with Brent settling at $102.31, after reports of additional U.S. military deployments to the Middle East and China's suspension of fuel-product exports added to supply concerns. At the same time, Fed officials have leaned against an immediate October hike after softer inflation, making today's employment report especially important: a moderate labor reading could reinforce the recent easing in near-term Fed expectations, while a strong payroll/wage combination could send yields back toward Thursday's highs. No reliable Nasdaq-100 futures quote available before the 06:00 Turkey-time cutoff was used.

catalysts.title: 1. September U.S. Employment Situation — 8:30 ET
catalysts.detail: This is the day's dominant scheduled catalyst. BLS is due to release September payrolls, unemployment and wage data at 8:30 ET. Expectations center on a material slowdown from August, with roughly 85,000–90,000 payroll gains and unemployment near 4.1%. With the 10-year having just touched 5.342%, Nasdaq's reaction may depend less on whether jobs are simply 'good' or 'bad' and more on whether the report pushes Treasury yields higher or lower. A strong payroll/wage combination would risk reviving tightening expectations; a moderate report without a sharp unemployment deterioration would be the cleaner outcome for growth stocks.

catalysts.title: 2. Oil / Iran / Middle East supply risk — unscheduled
catalysts.detail: Energy remains a direct Nasdaq macro catalyst because it is feeding inflation expectations and the bond selloff. Brent settled above $102 Thursday after reports that the U.S. was adding military assets in the Middle East and China halted fuel-product exports. Any escalation or credible diplomatic progress can move crude, inflation expectations and Treasury yields quickly enough to overwhelm the scheduled data signal.

catalysts.title: 3. Tesla Q3 deliveries — timing not formally fixed
catalysts.detail: Tesla is expected to report third-quarter production and deliveries today. The company-compiled analyst consensus published ahead of the release is around 462,000 vehicles. Tesla is a major Nasdaq-100 weight and the release can materially affect mega-cap/AI risk appetite, although the market increasingly values the company on autonomy, robotics and AI as well as vehicle volumes.

watchIntoOpen: What I’d watch into the open: the best Nasdaq scenario is a payroll report that shows orderly labor-market cooling, keeps unemployment contained, and pulls the 10-year decisively away from Thursday's 5.34% extreme while semiconductor leadership remains firm. The more dangerous scenario is a strong jobs/wages print that restarts the long-end selloff, especially if crude stays above $100 or geopolitical headlines push it higher. A superficially weak jobs number is not automatically bullish either: if unemployment rises sharply enough to trigger growth fears, lower yields may not translate cleanly into higher technology stocks. The first confirmation after 8:30 ET should therefore be the joint reaction of the 2-year and 10-year yields, Nasdaq futures, and semiconductor leadership rather than the payroll headline alone.
keyTimes: The U.S. cash market opens at 9:30 ET / 16:30 Istanbul. The critical scheduled event is the September Employment Situation at 8:30 ET / 15:30 Istanbul, one hour before the open. Tesla's Q3 delivery report is also expected today, but no exact release time was treated as confirmed by the cutoff. Oil and Middle East headlines remain live catalysts throughout the session. This is informational, not a trading recommendation.
